newsitem.title: UK: Unichem says won't raise Lloyds Chemist bid.
newsitem.headline: Unichem says won't raise Lloyds Chemist bid.

text.p: British drugs wholesaler Unichem Plc said on Monday it would not raise its offer for Lloyds Chemists Plc, declaring its bid final.
Unichem's statement came after its German rival, Gehe AG, raised its bid for LLoyds last Friday in a move that analysts predicted would be a knock-out blow in the year-long bidding battle.

Unichem, urging Lloyds' shareholders to accept its offer, said it expected pre-tax profits excluding the costs of the bid to rise eight percent in 1996 to more than 53.5 million pounds ($89.91 million).
The company said fully diluted earnings per share before bid costs would rise six percent to more than 20.2p and the final net dividend would be 5.8p per share, giving 8.8p for the year.
The company said the estimated results reflected further growth in sales and profits from every division. Group sales were expected to have risen by five percent.

The company said British wholesaling sales were expected to have grown by five percent, with second-half growth of eight percent and flat operating margins. In the retail pharmacy division, sales were expected to have risen 18 percent with a "material" increase in operating margins. ($1=.5950 Pound)
